Byte +5 bit 1 is confirmed (MinecraftKeyboardManager::isFocused at 0x395854: ldrb [r0,#5]; and #2; lsrs #1; it is vtable slot 5 of .?AVMinecraftKeyboardManager@@). BUT the fact's note says the ARM MinecraftKeyboardManager vtable is 0x0135d010; that is .?AVKeyboardManager@@, the abstract base (all slots _purecall), which no live object has as its vptr. The correct vtable to compare against x86 image+0x01569eac is 0x0135cfcc (also what client_state.keyboardmanager_vtable says). Using 0x135d010 would leave text_input_active permanently FALSE.

0x589590 copies the std::function with vtable[0] (_Copy) into a heap delegate and hands it to the dispatcher RunAsync (vtable +0x20); the cell patch is invoked wherever the dispatcher later runs it. Threading beyond that not verified (same caveat as the finder).

missing: text_input_active gate: the finder note used the wrong ARM keyboard vtable (0x135d010, abstract); it must be 0x0135cfcc (see input.text_focus_flag verdict). The porter needs this exact constant for refresh_relative_mouse_from_client_128.

queue_keyboard_event key-up path: stock onKeyUp 0x625d64 only enqueues a KeyCodeItem when controller[0xc9+key] is set; the x86 host always enqueues. No ARM change needed, but the hid_key_held_table fact should say so; the host win32_key_down[] autorepeat filter keeps behaviour equivalent.
Stock command consumer 0x626806 requires controller byte +0x25 == 0 before acting on command 1; not in any fact (harmless to the host, which clears +0x28 itself).

TextItem consumer (game-side drain of the adapter vector at +0x38) was not located by the finder or by me; the only evidence that the per-seq string array at controller+0x1f4 is unnecessary is that the x86 host works without it and TextItem owns its own std::string copy.

RVA_128_MOUSE_EVENT_FACTORY correspondence: the ARM exe has four sibling factories 0x62a128 (int,int,int,short,short), 0x62a174 (MultitouchItem), 0x62a1bc, 0x62a208; x86 0x8d6500 is only matched positionally. Any of the three MouseItem variants builds an identical item as long as argument widths are respected, so this is not a blocker.
